scope.target: population scalar mean squared error under the declared benchmark law, conditional on all development

sampling.sampling_law: independent episodes with replacement, independent of development
sampling.iid_premise: The statistical guarantee assumes genuine iid draws from the stipulated episode law. A deterministic pseudorandom implementation and distinct stream names do not themselves prove this premise.
external_freeze_bindings: the three complete selected predictor artifacts and canonical predictions on all 16 supported histories
the unchanged calibration reservation, stream identity, implementation, and prescribed count
development data identities and all selection decisions

confidence.conditional_statement: Under the stated premises, P_Cal[every reported valid endpoint U_m covers R_m(D), simultaneously over the fixed family | D] >= 19/20. If all three endpoints are available, the reported simultaneous statement covers all three risks.
confidence.availability_interpretation: The probability is conditional on development only, not additionally conditional on numerical availability, requirement acceptance, or a favorable result. Numerical failure yields an unavailable report, not a selected retry.
confidence.partially_available_statement: If only some numerical endpoints are established, the same fixed allocation gives simultaneous coverage of those reported endpoints; retain every unavailable candidate in the report and do not redistribute its allocation.

loss.name: ordinary_scalar_squared_error
loss.prediction_interpretation: Each finite canonical binary64 prediction is its exact represented rational value, recovered without decimal approximation from its canonical hexadecimal value or exact integer ratio.
loss.target_interpretation: Use the benchmark's exact rational observation values 0, 1/4, 3/4, and 1.
loss.loss_formula: ell_i = (y_i - f(x_i))^2, with subtraction and squaring performed in exact rational arithmetic
loss.invalid_input_action: certificate_unavailable for any nonfinite or out-of-range prediction, unsupported target, wrong count, missing record, or unverified frozen-prediction identity
loss.duplicate_handling: Prediction computation may be cached by a verified supported history, but all 4096 episode occurrences contribute separately to the exact loss mean.

endpoint.continuous_conventions: A zero-weight term is zero without evaluating its logarithm; a positive numerator over a zero denominator has infinite divergence.
endpoint.q_equals_one: Return the exact endpoint U=1 and the exact bracket [1,1] without evaluating a logarithm.
endpoint.q_equals_zero: For p<1, evaluate kl(0||p) = log(1/(1-p)), equivalently -log(1-p); if negating a logarithm interval, reverse its endpoints. Do not evaluate log(0).
endpoint.monotonicity: For q<1, kl(q||p) is continuous and strictly increasing for p in (q,1), equals zero at p=q, and tends to infinity as p tends to 1. Its upper root is unique.

verified_logarithm.arithmetic: arbitrary-precision integers and exact rational arithmetic only; every floor and ceiling is exact integer division
verified_logarithm.range_reduction: Find the integer a and rational u with x=2^a*u and 1<=u<2 using integer bit lengths and exact comparisons, never a floating logarithm.
verified_logarithm.series_variable: z=(u-1)/(u+1), so 0<=z<1/3; use z=1/3 separately for log(2)
verified_logarithm.series_term_count: M=b at working precision b bits
verified_logarithm.fixed_grid: D=2^b; every interval endpoint in the series calculation is an integer divided by D
verified_logarithm.zero_argument_in_series: If z=0, return the exact series logarithm interval [0,0].
verified_logarithm.power_initialization: L_0=floor(D*z), H_0=ceil(D*z), so L_0/D <= z <= H_0/D
verified_logarithm.term_accumulation: For j=0,...,M-1, add floor(2*L_j/(2*j+1)) to A and ceil(2*H_j/(2*j+1)) to B, starting from A=B=0.
verified_logarithm.power_recurrence: For each required next term, set L_(j+1)=floor(L_j*z^2) and H_(j+1)=ceil(H_j*z^2), with the products and divisions evaluated exactly.
verified_logarithm.series_interval: Return [A/D, (B+ceil(D*3/(4*(2*M+1)*9^M)))/D]. Directed rounding encloses every partial-sum term; the added nonnegative tail encloses all omitted terms.
verified_logarithm.range_recombination: Add the interval for log(u) to a times the interval for log(2); if a<0, reverse the endpoints of the multiplied log(2) interval.
verified_logarithm.cache_policy: Cache exact log(2) and log(60) intervals separately at each declared precision. Caching must not change any rational endpoint.
verified_logarithm.unverified_logarithm_use: prohibited in endpoint construction or verification

upper_root_algorithm.initial_bracket: For q<1, set L=q and H=1. The lower-side proof is kl(q||q)=0<log(60)/4096; H=1 is an analytic upper boundary.
upper_root_algorithm.trial: If H-L is greater than 2^-80, set p=(L+H)/2 exactly and evaluate F(p) using interval logarithms, first at 128 bits, then 256 and 512 only if necessary.
upper_root_algorithm.interval_formula: If KL is enclosed by [K_low,K_high] and log(60) by [C_low,C_high], enclose F(p) by [4096*K_low-C_high,4096*K_high-C_low]. Nonnegative q and 1-q multiply their logarithm intervals without reversing endpoints.
upper_root_algorithm.upper_move: If the lower endpoint of the F interval is >=0, replace H by p and save the precision and inequality witness. This proves 4096*kl(q||H) >= log(60).
upper_root_algorithm.lower_move: Otherwise, if the upper endpoint of the F interval is <=0, replace L by p and save the precision and inequality witness. This proves 4096*kl(q||L) <= log(60).
upper_root_algorithm.ambiguous_comparison: If neither comparison is proved, keep both bracket endpoints unchanged and try the next precision at the same p. At 512 bits, an unresolved comparison returns certificate_unavailable; it never guesses a sign or repeatedly retries without a bound.
upper_root_algorithm.near_root_policy: Even a trial exactly at the real root, or arbitrarily close to it, need not admit a finite strict interval sign decision. Successful narrowing is not assumed. A valid bracket is retained diagnostically, but no endpoint is reported under this protocol unless the target width and independent checks are established.
upper_root_algorithm.stopping_rule: Return U=H as an exact rational only when 0<=q<=L<=H<=1, H-L<=2^-80, and the independent endpoint check succeeds. Since the initial width is at most one, 80 successful halvings suffice.
upper_root_algorithm.returned_endpoint_rounding: H is already an outward upper endpoint. Preserve it exactly; do not convert it to a binary floating root.
upper_root_algorithm.trivial_upper_boundary: H=1 is verified analytically. It is an allowed reported endpoint only when the same target-width rule holds, including q=1.

independent_numerical_check.scope: Recompute the exact empirical mean and directly check the saved bracket endpoints and their inequality witnesses; do not call the root-search routine.
independent_numerical_check.lower_endpoint: Accept L=q analytically; otherwise require q<L<1 and a fresh exact interval evaluation at the recorded precision proving 4096*kl(q||L) <= log(60).
independent_numerical_check.upper_endpoint: Accept H=1 analytically; otherwise require q<H<1 and a fresh exact interval evaluation at the recorded precision proving 4096*kl(q||H) >= log(60).
independent_numerical_check.width_check: Compare H-L with the exact rational 2^-80.
independent_numerical_check.numerical_scope: These checks certify logarithm enclosures and endpoint direction for the actual stored prediction values. They do not certify an ideal real-arithmetic Gaussian KAHM map or establish the iid sampling premise.

work_limits.exact_empirical_risk_bound_reason: A binary64 value in [0,1] has dyadic denominator at most 2^1074; an exact squared loss has denominator at most 2^2148; division by 4096=2^12 gives at most 2^2160.
work_limits.budget_enforcement: Check integer bit lengths and the cumulative series-term counter. If a declared bound, arithmetic check, or required invariant is violated, stop that numerical certificate with certificate_unavailable and preserve the failure record.

reporting.exact_rational_record: Store exact q, bracket endpoints, logarithm witnesses, and U using base-10 integer strings for numerator and positive denominator; never round through JSON floating-point numbers.
reporting.prediction_record: Retain canonical hexadecimal binary64 predictions and all calibration episode identities and outcomes.
reporting.outward_decimal_rule: For U=A/B, calculate J=ceil(10^18*A/B) by integer division and format J/10^18 as a decimal string with exactly 18 fractional digits. This display is an upper bound on U.
reporting.decision_rule: Compare exact U=A/B with 1/10 by testing 10*A<=B; the displayed decimal is not used for the decision.

statuses.requirement_met: all premises and checks established and exact U<=1/10
statuses.unresolved: all premises and checks established and exact U>1/10; this does not establish that the risk exceeds the tolerance
statuses.certificate_unavailable: a required premise, identity, input, work-limit, numerical enclosure, root-width, or independent check is not established

reporting.unavailable_candidate_visibility: Report every frozen candidate, including every failure; leave its endpoint null and retain a reason code and available diagnostics.
reporting.claim_after_selection: Any candidate meeting the requirement may be chosen within this fixed three-member family without an extra allocation; no additional searched or revised predictor is covered by that statement.

change_control.scope: one predeclared primary calibration of one frozen three-member family
change_control.after_calibration_prediction_change: Requires a new freeze and untouched calibration, with repeated-attempt selection accounted for.
change_control.numerical_recalculation: Archived calibration may be reused only after endpoint equivalence or conservativeness is established; retain the original results and audit trail.
change_control.sampling_or_budget_retry: Do not replace the prescribed calibration data or silently alter this fixed protocol in response to outcomes or numerical failure.

source_basis.use: bounded iid fitted-loss upper endpoint, conditional union bound, shared calibration across candidates, and conservative numerical enclosures
range-reduced atanh logarithm tail bound, exact dyadic interval recurrences, verified root brackets, direct outer-endpoint checking, and bounded work
